title: Why You Feel a Phantom Phone Vibration

vo.en: Your phone isn't vibrating in your pocket.

visual.description: Close up of a man feeling his empty pants pocket with a look of confusion.

vo.en: It’s a glitch called phantom vibration syndrome. Your brain is playing a trick on your sense of touch.

visual.description: Abstract shot of brain neural network animation or glowing synapses.

vo.en: Constant phone checking creates a new habit. Your nervous system is now on high alert for notifications.

visual.description: A man constantly glancing at his wrist and checking his phone screen.

vo.en: When your leg muscles twitch or fabric rubs against your skin, your brain misinterprets the physical sensation.

visual.description: Macro shot of fabric moving against skin or human muscle twitch.

vo.en: It expects the vibration, so it creates one. You have essentially trained yourself to hallucinate signals.

visual.description: Man looking down at his pocket, thinking he feels something but finding nothing.

vo.en: So when you reach down to check again, remember that...

visual.description: A hand reaching into a pocket and pulling out nothing, then pausing.
